summary: Design agent systems by choosing orchestration patterns, tools, and memory, and by deciding where code should handle work instead of the LLM.
highYield: Orchestration patterns: sequential pipeline, parallel, coordinator-worker, and group chat / hierarchical; know when single-agent suffices.
Frameworks: Semantic Kernel (plugins, planners, agents), AutoGen (conversable agents, group chat), OpenAI Agents SDK (handoffs, guardrails), LangChain.
Agent anatomy: system prompt/persona, tools (function calling), memory (short- vs long-term), and knowledge (RAG).
Agent-to-agent and tool integration: A2A protocol for agent communication and MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tools/context.
Design rule: use deterministic code for deterministic steps and reserve the LLM for judgment/reasoning.
memoryAids: Patterns = Sequential, Parallel, Coordinator-Worker, Group Chat.

summary: Build agents on Azure AI Foundry Agent Service and frameworks, wiring tools, knowledge grounding, and orchestration together.
highYield: Azure AI Foundry: Agent Service (managed agents, threads, tools), projects, and model deployments (GPT-4o/o-series, embeddings).
Agent tools: function calling, code interpreter, file search, Azure AI Search grounding, Bing grounding, and OpenAPI tools.
Semantic Kernel: plugins split into native functions (code) and prompt functions (LLM); AutoGen workflows for multi-agent conversations.
Azure OpenAI: standard vs provisioned throughput, token/context management, Assistants API vs Agent Service.
Hosting/state: Foundry Agents SDK, Azure Container Apps for hosting, Cosmos DB for agent memory and state.
memoryAids: Tool types = function, code interpreter, file search, Azure AI Search.
SK plugin = native function + prompt function.
Foundry Agent Service = managed agents + threads + tools.

domain: Evaluate, optimize, and monitor multi-agent solutions
summary: Measure agent quality with LLM evaluations and monitor runtime behavior with tracing and observability, then tune prompts/RAG.
highYield: Evaluation metrics: groundedness, relevance, coherence, fluency, similarity - measured via the Azure AI Evaluation SDK.
Adversarial/red-team testing, A/B testing, and golden datasets for regression.
Observability: OpenTelemetry, Azure AI Foundry tracing (GenAI trace), and distributed tracing across agents.
Optimization: prompt engineering, RAG tuning (chunking, top-k, embeddings), fine-tuning vs RAG, and token/cost optimization.
Runtime monitoring: latency, token usage, error rates, and safety (content filters, prompt shields).
memoryAids: Eval metrics = Groundedness, Relevance, Coherence, Fluency, Similarity.
RAG for knowledge, fine-tune for style/format, prompt for quick fixes.
Trace = follow one request across all agents.

domain: Secure, govern, and deploy multi-agent solutions
summary: Deploy agents to production with responsible AI guardrails, managed identity and RBAC, and CI/CD to managed compute.
highYield: Security: managed identity, RBAC, Key Vault for secrets, content safety filters, and prompt shields (jailbreak + indirect injection defense).
Governance: Azure Policy, tagging, Microsoft Purview, and Responsible AI principles (fairness, safety, privacy, transparency, accountability).
Deployment targets: Azure Container Apps, App Service, AKS, and Foundry online endpoints / provisioned throughput.
CI/CD: GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps with ACR, blue-green/canary releases, and deployment slots.
Threat model: prompt injection (direct/indirect), data exfiltration, and tool-use abuse - enforce least-privilege tools.
memoryAids: Prompt Shields = jailbreak + indirect injection defense.
Managed identity + Key Vault = no secrets in code or agents.
Responsible AI = Fairness, Reliability, Privacy, Inclusiveness, Transparency, Accountability.
